summary: The routing page (patchbay.c) is the only part of RadioS that uses PulseAudio server-side features. It uses introspection of sinks, sources (including monitor_of_sink) and sink-inputs (application.name / application.process.binary), creates module-null-sink and module-remap-source for the "Sanal ses arayüzü" block and its virtual microphone, calls move-sink-input to move another app's stream into that sink, subscribes to events, and cleans up stale modules after a crash. Its record and playback streams use FLOAT32 48 kHz stereo with ADJUST_LATENCY|DONT_MOVE, and it asks for the PipeWire "Manager" role. channel_input.c opens its own private Pulse connection per channel input for sound-card capture; its network path is FFmpeg and portable. Pulse naming rules (radios_virtual_<id>, "<sink>.monitor", "_mic") are baked into routing_graph.c implicit() and the SDBASE validator desktop_api.py. The recommended Windows design has six parts. (1) A shared internal audio-host layer (audio_host.h) with WASAPI, fixture and optional Pulse implementations, used by the engine backend, the patchbay and channel inputs so device ids are identical everywhere. (2) A naming contract: endpoints are named by their IMMDevice::GetId() string, a render endpoint's loopback is "<id>.monitor", and "@default", "@talk" and radios_virtual_<id> are kept, so the C and Python loop validators work unchanged. (3) Per-application capture uses process loopback (ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync with VIRTUAL_AUDIO_DEVICE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK, INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE and an agile completion handler on an MTA thread). Applications are listed through IAudioSessionManager2 sessions (PID → exe name and display name). Identity is PID plus creation time, and an open process handle pins the PID and detects exit. (4) The RG_VIRTUAL block becomes an application-capture block on Windows. It creates no endpoint and moves nothing (the app stays audible on its own output), as_microphone is not supported, and cabled input is summed internally. (5) Shared-mode WASAPI capture, loopback and render run on per-stream MMCSS I/O threads that feed the existing lock-free rings, with all timing constants unchanged. (6) A deterministic fixture audio host (RADIOS_AUDIO_HOST=fixture:json) replaces the private PulseAudio/pactl/pacat test fixtures; real-WASAPI tests are opt-in. The MSYS2 UCRT64 headers have everything needed except audioclientactivationparams.h, which must be declared by hand; libmmdevapi.a exports ActivateAudioInterfaceAsync, and MSYS2 FFmpeg 9.0.2 includes srt. Validators must accept both path styles for the recorder folder (POSIX and Windows drive/UNC) and must forbid <>:"|?* in the file prefix (":" would create an NTFS alternate data stream). I also found latent bugs in the current code: 64- and 80-byte buffers in routing_graph.c implicit() truncate device names, and secure_free() uses a memset that the compiler may remove.
files_touched: src/audio/audio_host_pulse.c (new, optional: existing Pulse code moved)
database/SDBASE/src/sdbase/desktop_api.py (recorder folder/prefix validation, optional virtual app fields)
CMakeLists.txt (radios_audio sources/libs, XTST/GDK_BACKEND only on Linux, test env)
key_decisions: Introduce a shared internal audio host API (src/audio/audio_host.h) with WASAPI, fixture and optional Pulse implementations. Engine backend, patchbay and channel inputs must all use its device enumeration so persisted ids are identical everywhere.

Device naming contract: endpoint name = IMMDevice::GetId() verbatim, with no prefix. The loopback of a render endpoint = '<render id>.monitor'. '@default' resolves eConsole at open, '@talk' is unchanged, and 'radios_virtual_<id>' stays reserved. This keeps routing_graph.c implicit() and desktop_api.py implicit() unchanged.
Missing saved devices stay selected and are shown as unavailable, using the friendly name of the unplugged endpoint. There is never an automatic substitution by name or by default device.

Per-application capture uses process loopback (INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE). Apps are listed from IAudioSessionManager2 sessions, deduplicated by PID, with system sounds and RadioS itself filtered out. RadioSPatchApplication.index = PID. Identity = PID + creation time, pinned by an open SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle. When the app exits, capture stops and there is no automatic re-capture.
Process-loopback support is detected by a runtime probe, never by version check. If unsupported, a clear Turkish error is shown and there is no fallback to mixed endpoint loopback.

On Windows RG_VIRTUAL becomes an application-capture block: no endpoint is created and nothing is moved, so the app stays audible on its own output. as_microphone is unsupported; the JSON field is kept, and the UI explains that a virtual-cable driver plus an OUTPUT block is needed. Cabled input is summed internally into the block output.

RadioS never changes host audio state: no session volume/mute changes, no per-app device routing (undocumented IAudioPolicyConfig is rejected), no default-device changes, and communications ducking is opted out via SetDuckingPreference.

Streams are 48 kHz float stereo at the API boundary: shared mode with AUTOCONVERTPCM|SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY, RadioS does its own mono duplication or swresample downmix, and endpoint loopback has a silent keep-alive render. There is one MMCSS 'Pro Audio' I/O thread per stream feeding the existing SPSC rings. Constants (PRIME/LIMIT/KEEP, 3 s open timeout, 5 s retry, 3 s resync) are unchanged.
All COM/WASAPI work happens on MTA host/I/O threads, never on the GTK STA thread. move_application only validates the PID, pins the process handle and records the binding.
The patchbay 10 ms worker uses a high-resolution waitable timer on Windows. The process-wide timeBeginPeriod(1) and power-throttling opt-out are requested from the startup owner.

Host spec string replaces pulse_server: NULL means $RADIOS_AUDIO_HOST (the Windows equivalent of PULSE_SERVER) or the system host; 'fixture:<json>' selects the fixture; 'none:' never connects. On Windows any 'unix:' spec counts as 'none:', so existing tests stay off host audio.

Recorder folder validation becomes platform-neutral in both the C and Python validators: POSIX absolute, Windows drive-absolute or UNC are accepted; \\?\, \\.\ and drive-relative paths are rejected. At runtime Windows requires a fully qualified path. The file prefix additionally rejects <>:"|?*, with defensive runtime sanitization.

Optional persisted selection hint for virtual blocks (application_binary, application_name). It only preselects the app combo; capture always needs the explicit operator click. PIDs, start times, session ids and indices are never persisted.

Testing: a deterministic in-process fixture audio host emulates endpoints, monitors, per-app process loopback, service stop/restart and app exit, and keeps the existing fixture device names. Real-WASAPI process-loopback acceptance is opt-in, uses a non-audible endpoint, and skips with 77 otherwise. The XTest graph test becomes a SendInput/SetCursorPos variant with DPI scaling.
risks: Process loopback is officially documented for Windows 10 build 20348+/Windows 11 and only works in practice from 2004 (19041). Behaviour (format, packets during silence, session-volume effect, elevated targets) must be confirmed in an early spike.

Product semantics change for 'Sanal ses arayüzü': no app move (the app is still heard on its own output), no virtual microphone, no RadioS device for other apps. This needs lead/UX sign-off; only a signed virtual audio driver would restore parity.
Apps using exclusive-mode WASAPI, ASIO or WDM-KS (common in DJ software) and DRM-protected content cannot be captured.
Endpoint ids can change after a driver reinstall or a USB port change, so saved selections become 'Kullanılamıyor'. By contract there is no automatic substitution.
Windows 15.6 ms timer granularity and Windows 11 power throttling when minimized can cause tick bursts and glitches unless high-resolution timers, MMCSS and the process-wide opt-outs are implemented.
Microphone privacy settings return E_ACCESSDENIED. Communications ducking could alter other apps' volume if not opted out. Opening a Bluetooth microphone switches the headset to HFP.
Endpoint loopback delivers no packets while silent; this needs a keep-alive render or tolerant priming.

There is no private audio server on Windows and CI usually has no audio endpoints, so the fixture host is mandatory. GUI pointer tests need an interactive desktop, foreground permission and correct per-monitor DPI scaling.

Shared Linux/Windows DB documents: a Linux recorder folder (/tmp/...) is valid in the document but unusable at runtime on Windows (a clear error is required). Old documents with ':' in the prefix become invalid under the new validator.
Any WASAPI/COM call that reaches the GTK STA thread, or an IMMNotificationClient callback that blocks, causes hard-to-debug hangs.
FFmpeg 9.0.2 (avformat 63) in MSYS2 may need API adjustments in channel_input.c. UDP/RTP listener inputs trigger a Windows Firewall prompt unless packaging adds a rule.

Latent bugs to fix on both OSes: routing_graph.c:139-142 truncates device names >63 bytes in loop detection; secure_free() memset can be optimized away. docs/ses-yonlendirme.md describes removed schema-1 behaviour.
cross_area_dependencies: audio-engine/backend (pulse_backend.c → WASAPI): must build on or share src/audio/audio_host.h enumeration so RadioSAudioSnapshot.inputs/outputs use the same ids (including '<id>.monitor' loopback entries, monitor=TRUE, monitors last). radios_audio_engine_new(realtime, NULL) must honour RADIOS_AUDIO_HOST (the fixture host) like libpulse honours PULSE_SERVER. Engine tap/line API (radios_audio_engine_tap_open/line_open) stays unchanged.

audio-output (src/audio/output.c): WAV recorder open on Windows: O_CLOEXEC does not exist (use _O_NOINHERIT), add O_BINARY, keep exclusive create, replace 0600 with an owner-only ACL via the platform layer, replace fsync with _commit/FlushFileBuffers, drop unistd.h. Also libcurl https Icecast needs a CA source (CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA or a bundled ca file).

platform layer (platform.h/.c): process identity/watch, fully-qualified path test, filename-part validation, owner-only ACL, MMCSS thread enter/leave, high-resolution sleep_until, MTA COM init, secure zero, Windows build query (see platform_api_needs).

application startup/manifest owner: process-wide timeBeginPeriod(1) and SetProcessInformation(ProcessPowerThrottling) opt-out of EXECUTION_SPEED and IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION; longPathAware manifest; GDK main thread stays OLE STA (no WASAPI there).

SDBASE (database/SDBASE/src/sdbase/desktop_api.py): platform-neutral recorder folder validation (POSIX, drive, UNC; reject \\?\, \\.\, drive-relative), prefix rejects <>:"|?*, optional virtual settings application_binary/application_name in _ROUTING_SETTINGS_OPTIONAL. The implicit() Pulse naming rules stay unchanged.

build/CMake owner: link ole32 uuid mmdevapi avrt winmm version shlwapi advapi32 for radios_audio on WIN32; no libpulse on WIN32; test_pulse_hotplug, XTST and GDK_BACKEND=x11 only on Linux; user32 for the Windows graph UI test; WASAPI TUs compiled with COBJMACROS/WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN/_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00.

test infrastructure owners (run_audio_ui.py, test_application_shutdown.py, application_shutdown_driver.c, tools/radios_database.py): switch from private PulseAudio/pactl/parec/pacat to fixture-host JSON with the same device names. Helpers from run_audio_routing.py move to a portable tests/audio_test_support.py.
UI/DJ owner (src/ui/dj.c): 'in:<device id>' choices are unchanged; show the friendly name of missing devices via the host describe function.
docs owner: update docs/ses-yonlendirme.md for Windows (WASAPI, process loopback limits, no virtual mic, radios.exe --profile routing, owner-only ACL).
packaging owner: optional Windows Firewall inbound rule for UDP/RTP/SRT listener inputs; optional CA bundle for curl.
platform_api_needs: gboolean radios_platform_process_start_time(guint32 pid, guint64 *start_time_100ns) — Windows: OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + GetProcessTimes creation FILETIME; POSIX: /proc/<pid>/stat starttime. FALSE if the process is gone or access is denied.

gboolean radios_platform_process_image(guint32 pid, gchar **basename_utf8, gchar **description_utf8) — Windows: QueryFullProcessImageNameW → basename (UTF-8, original case) and version-resource FileDescription (GetFileVersionInfoW/VerQueryValueW), either may be NULL; POSIX: /proc/<pid>/comm/exe. Caller g_free()s.

RadioSProcessWatch *radios_platform_process_watch_open(guint32 pid, guint64 expected_start_time, GError **error) — Windows: OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and verify the creation time equals expected (else error 'Uygulama kimliği değişti'); the handle pins the PID against reuse. POSIX: pidfd_open/kill(0) + start-time check.

gboolean radios_platform_process_watch_exited(RadioSProcessWatch *watch) — Windows: WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0) == WAIT_OBJECT_0; never blocks. void radios_platform_process_watch_close(RadioSProcessWatch *watch) closes the handle.

gboolean radios_platform_path_is_fully_qualified(const gchar *utf8_path) — Windows: TRUE only for 'X:\\…' / 'X:/…' or UNC '\\\\server\\share\\…'; FALSE for drive-relative 'X:foo', rooted '\\foo' or '/foo', '\\\\?\\' and '\\\\.\\' device paths. POSIX: g_path_is_absolute.

gboolean radios_platform_filename_part_valid(const gchar *utf8_part) — portable rule used for recorder prefixes: non-empty UTF-8, no control chars, none of / \\ < > : " | ? *, not starting with '.', no trailing space/dot; the same on all OSes so documents are portable.

gboolean radios_platform_restrict_to_owner(const gchar *utf8_path, gboolean directory, GError **error) — Windows: SetNamedSecurityInfoW with a protected DACL (current user full control + SYSTEM; directories with inheritance OI|CI); POSIX: chmod 0700/0600. gboolean radios_platform_path_is_owner_only(const gchar *utf8_path) — test helper replacing the 'st_mode & 0777 == 0600' assertion.

gpointer radios_platform_audio_thread_enter(const gchar *task) / void radios_platform_audio_thread_leave(gpointer token) — Windows: AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW(L"Pro Audio") / AvRevertMmThreadCharacteristics (avrt); POSIX: no-op (or best-effort priority).

void radios_platform_sleep_until(gint64 monotonic_deadline_us) — Windows: per-thread high-resolution waitable timer (CreateWaitableTimerExW with CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION, falling back to a normal timer), absolute deadline relative to g_get_monotonic_time(); returns immediately if the deadline has passed; POSIX: clock_nanosleep/g_usleep. Used for the patchbay 10 ms clock.

void radios_platform_realtime_process_setup(void) — called once at startup: Windows timeBeginPeriod(1) and SetProcessInformation(GetCurrentProcess(), ProcessPowerThrottling, {Version=1, ControlMask=EXECUTION_SPEED|IGNORE_TIMER_RESOLUTION, StateMask=0}); POSIX: no-op.

gboolean radios_platform_com_init_mta(void) / void radios_platform_com_uninit(void) — Windows: CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_MULTITHREADED), treat S_FALSE as success and RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE as an error (only uninit if init succeeded); POSIX: no-op. Called at the start/end of the patchbay control thread, channel-input workers and host threads.
void radios_platform_secure_zero(gpointer data, gsize size) — Windows: SecureZeroMemory; POSIX: explicit_bzero/volatile loop. Replaces memset in patchbay secure_free() and routing.c start_job_free().
gboolean radios_platform_windows_build(guint *major, guint *minor, guint *build) — RtlGetVersion (ntdll) for diagnostics and error messages only, never for feature gating; FALSE on POSIX.

Test-only (tests/ helper, not production platform.h): gboolean radios_test_pointer_move(gint x_logical, gint y_logical, GdkWindow *ref) — scales by gdk_window_get_scale_factor and calls SetCursorPos on Windows or XTestFakeMotionEvent on X11; gboolean radios_test_pointer_button(guint button, gboolean pressed) — SendInput MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN/UP vs XTestFakeButtonEvent; gboolean radios_test_pointer_get(gint *x, gint *y) — GetCursorPos vs XQueryPointer.
